purpose: Ten additional visual proposals extending the sixteen-study gallery
continuity: Text prompts based on existing gallery art direction and confirmed design; no image attached to generation calls.

images.title: The assignment before the descent
images.alt: Researchers gather around a lit assignment board in a cramped company briefing room overlooking the sphere chamber.
images.caption: A proposed briefing space puts the daily assignment between company routine and the immense excavation outside. Pinned diagrams suggest instructions without settling the mission interface.
images.question: What detail in a routine assignment would tell the team that today's shift is different?
images.scene: Interior company briefing room before the workday. Three yellow-suited researchers stand around a battered cork board holding blank paper sheets, a simple abstract sphere cross-section drawing and an old clock with no legible digits. An enamel table with mugs and gloves, coat hooks, scuffed linoleum, low sickly fluorescent ceiling. Through a broad grimy window behind them, a small distant reflective sphere and scaffold lights hang in a vast chamber. The team is viewed from slightly above the table, gestures subdued, ordinary workplace administration against impossible scale. No readable writing.

images.title: Evidence in the drawers
images.alt: Open specimen drawers contain glass, piping, tile and fibrous office samples under a research lamp.
images.caption: A proposed material archive turns excavation layers into comparable evidence. Ordered drawers explore how the team might recognize familiar samples and notice one that does not belong.
images.question: Which material difference should be clear by sight before a researcher uses any instrument?
images.scene: Intimate overhead three-quarter still-life of a company research archive: a battered flat-file cabinet pulled open to reveal separate foam-lined trays of mirror-glass shards, corroded pipe cross-sections, white pool tile, acoustic office fiber and curled wallpaper. One gloved yellow sleeve gently holds a sample with metal tongs under a plain articulated task lamp. Blank index tabs, small magnifying lens, calipers and specimen envelopes. A shard reflects a fluorescent corridor instead of the desk. Warm lamp against cool green institutional shadows, precise tactile materials, not a fantasy treasure collection.

images.title: Below the working face
images.alt: Two researchers survey the underside of the sphere from a suspended industrial cradle above a dark shaft.
images.caption: A suspended survey cradle explores another view of the excavation's scale. Its access method and any work beneath the sphere remain proposals, alongside the established scaffolding system.
images.question: What information would make taking a survey below the main platform worth the journey?
images.scene: Dramatic wide upward-looking view from a lower maintenance ledge toward the underside of the immense mirror sphere above an abyss. Two tiny yellow-suited researchers occupy a practical rectangular industrial inspection cradle with guardrails, four taut suspension cables leading to a visible overhead beam, and a bright portable lamp angled upward. The sphere's lower surface reflects compressed rooms in curved bands. Large negative space of dark haze beneath, monumental sphere occupying upper frame, scaffolding rings far above. Believable rigging, no flying craft or free-floating platforms.

images.title: One reflection stays behind
images.alt: A departing researcher is reflected standing still in a large glass shard beside an otherwise empty platform.
images.caption: A delayed reflection proposes an anomaly made from the first layer's familiar material. The discrepancy invites observation without establishing a time-loop rule or explaining the collapse.
images.question: How long should a reflection disagree before players can be certain it is a clue?
images.scene: Quiet close-medium scene on an empty excavation platform beside the sphere: a tall broken mirror-glass fragment rests securely in an industrial padded rack. A yellow-suited researcher is walking away into the left background, while the reflection in the foreground shard shows the same researcher standing still facing it, back to viewer, subtly different posture. Use a readable discrepancy in pose, no duplicate physical person. The shard reflects a mundane fluorescent corridor and railing. Cold amber industrial light, mirror silver, generous stillness, no glowing eyes, monsters or effects.

images.title: A signal across the gap
images.alt: Two researchers install a compact wired relay on a scaffold while a distant work lamp shines across the chamber.
images.caption: Installing unusual equipment is part of the assignment direction. This wired relay is one possible visual treatment, with its purpose, placement rules and cooperative actions still open.
images.question: Which part of installing special equipment should ask teammates to communicate across the chamber?
images.scene: Medium side view of two yellow-suited researchers installing a compact rugged wired signal relay on a scaffold upright overlooking the chasm. One fastens a mechanical clamp at chest height, the other carefully feeds a thick cable from a grounded reel, hands clearly occupied with separate tasks. Relay has a small analog meter, short loop antenna and three dim indicator bulbs, no legible marks. Across the chamber a lone work lamp and matching installation position are visible. Sphere's curved reflective edge only a sliver at right, believable bolts, railings, worn cable jackets, warm practical lights and cool distance. No futuristic laser communications.

images.title: Wait for the light to pass
images.alt: Researchers hide behind a hotel linen cart while the shadow of a tall angular creature crosses a distant doorway.
images.caption: A proposed evasion encounter uses a mundane service alcove and a distant silhouette. Cover, timing and the warning cue need design; the image does not establish a new enemy behavior.
images.question: What cue lets a cautious team judge when it is safe to leave cover?
images.scene: Restrained suspense inside a Terror Hotel event corridor. Camera low in a service alcove behind a loaded linen cart; two yellow-suited researchers crouch quietly with tools lowered. Far down the burgundy-carpeted passage, a tall thin nonhuman angular SHADOW crosses the light spilling from a side doorway; no creature close-up. A swinging amber wall lamp creates a long sharp moving shadow on the wallpaper. A separate visible side route near the researchers offers a readable exit option. Tarnished brass, folded sheets, worn paint, dim amber and cool blue shadows. No gore, no attack, no jump-scare face, no bright eyes.

images.title: Back into the same hallway
images.alt: A researcher steps through an ordinary door from a blue tiled event space into a yellow hallway where a teammate and cart wait.
images.caption: Event doors are intended to return players to the main hallway. This transition study explores recognizable landmarks and the uneasy contrast between an excursion and the ordinary route back.
images.question: Which landmark should confirm the team has returned, and which small detail could remain uncertain?
images.scene: Wide carefully composed threshold scene viewed from a mundane yellow Backrooms main hallway. An ordinary open door reveals a cool blue tiled event space with a shallow pool and geometric columns, impossibly deep. One yellow-suited researcher steps out carrying a small sample case; another waits several meters away beside a scuffed utility go-kart parked at a familiar pillar. In the warm corridor foreground, a bent radiator pipe and a patch of mismatched carpet serve as distinctive landmarks. Cool light spills through the doorway, no glowing magical portal. Emphasize crossing back to company routine, ordinary door thickness and mundane architecture.

images.title: The morning arrangement
images.alt: A company break-room table holds two identical mugs with matching coffee stains beside a researcher's gloved hand.
images.caption: A repeated morning could be recognized through small arrangements rather than spectacle. This still-life proposes a memory cue; exact reset behavior and persistence remain undecided.
images.question: What everyday arrangement would players remember accurately enough to recognize a repeated day?
images.scene: Unsettling mundane still-life in an empty company break room, close waist-height camera: two identical chipped enamel mugs sit side by side on a scratched table, each surrounded by an uncannily identical irregular dried coffee ring and the same three crumbs. One yellow-gloved hand hovers above them as if noticing the duplication. A folded yellow work jacket on a chair, old electric kettle and fluorescent strip reflection in the background. Geometric repetition but no mirror between the objects, no collage or split screen, no floating effects. Muted nicotine yellow, gray-green and cold morning light. Focus on exact small repeated details and hesitant human gesture.

images.title: Something the drill did not make
images.alt: Researchers examine an ambiguous curled nonhuman specimen exposed among pipes and broken concrete.
images.caption: The excavation can reveal creatures or carcasses. This restrained recovery study explores an ambiguous nonhuman shape before deciding its identity, scientific value or connection to the living core.
images.question: What visible evidence should help the team distinguish a dormant threat from an inert specimen?
images.scene: Medium-wide investigative excavation scene in a Utility Halls pocket: broken concrete and pipes expose a small curled nonhuman chitinous husk, about the size of a dog, with a continuous ridged shell and a few folded insectlike appendages. It is clearly an ambiguous dried specimen, not a human body, no wounds or blood. Two company researchers in yellow suits examine it without touching: one directs a work lamp, the other opens a padded transport crate using metal tongs held back. The heavy auger is switched off on its support. Concrete dust, dim green tube lighting and warm examination light. Mystery and careful observation, not action horror.

images.title: The clue outside the window
images.alt: A desk monitor shows simple company software while a recovered tile fragment matches a shape in a printed diagram.
images.caption: Computer Research connects field discoveries with ordinary company software. This desk study proposes a clue shared across a sample, a paper diagram and an on-screen window; the actual puzzle remains open.
images.question: Which clue should require looking away from the screen to understand the research task?
images.scene: Close over-the-shoulder research desk scene, one yellow-suited researcher partly cropped at left, focus on a battered beige desktop monitor and physical evidence below. Screen shows mundane gray office software with unlabeled folder icons and an abstract L-shaped grid puzzle in a small window, no readable text. A recovered white pool-tile fragment on the desk shares a distinctive missing-corner silhouette with a simple printed diagram taped beside the monitor. Ordinary keyboard, coiled mouse cable, magnifying glass, one muted task lamp. A dark observation window behind the desk reflects the pattern of ceiling lights. Strong triangle of screen, artifact and diagram; no holograms or sci-fi HUD.
